claims.text: Program.cs lines 22-41 read Jwt:SigningKey (throwing if missing) and set IssuerSigningKey to a SymmetricSecurityKey from it with ValidateIssuerSigningKey; JwtTokenService signs with the same Jwt:SigningKey (HmacSha256).
Configuration is read at startup, so a changed signing key takes effect only when the API starts again.
claims.source_hint: Program.cs reads the key once into a local before building the app; foundation.l1.env-and-config (environment copied at process start)

claims.text: Anyone holding an HMAC signing key can create a token with arbitrary claims whose signature the API accepts; a short key can be recovered offline by trying candidates against one real token.
After the API restarts with a different key, tokens signed with the old key are rejected (401); restoring the old key makes them accepted again.
claims.source_hint: generator check: POST /api/v1/orders with an old token -> 401 under a new key, 201 after restoring

claims.text: JWT_SIGNING_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48) docker compose up -d api recreates the api with a different key (shell variable overrides .env); in the app, ordering then shows 'Failed: Exception: failed to create order (401)'; docker compose up -d api restores the .env key.
claims.source_hint: generator check on the running lab; Docker docs: Compose variable precedence; frontend.l1.creating-an-order

claims.text: A leaked signing key exposes every account at once, wherever requests come from; the key must be long and random.
